claims.text: Higher initial short-range chemical order will reduce surface segregation in near-equiatomic multi-element nanoparticles at 773–1173 K.
Higher initial short-range chemical order will reduce microstructural degradation in these nanoparticles at 773–1173 K.
Local chemical correlations are the primary determinant of structural and compositional stability under reactive environments.
Near-equiatomic multi-element nanoparticles can be prepared with controlled high and low levels of short-range chemical order while retaining identical composition.
Short-range chemical order can be quantified through site occupancies and local coordination.
High-temperature short-range ordering occurs in multi-element alloys.
Persistent short-range ordering slows atomic interdiffusion.
Suppressed surface segregation mitigates phase decomposition.
Suppressed surface segregation mitigates morphology changes associated with high-temperature performance loss.
High-order nanoparticles will undergo smaller changes in particle diameter than low-order nanoparticles under otherwise identical high-temperature exposure.
High-order nanoparticles will develop less composition inhomogeneity than low-order nanoparticles.
High-order nanoparticles will form fewer secondary phases than low-order nanoparticles.
Low-order nanoparticles will show greater chemical and structural instability under the same service conditions.
Above roughly 1200 K, different equilibrium phases may develop regardless of initial short-range order.
Extremely high reactive-gas partial pressures may cause oxidation or segregation regardless of initial short-range order.
Extended dwell times may cause oxidation or segregation regardless of initial short-range order.
Controlled annealing can generate two nanoparticle populations differing principally in verified short-range order.

Equivalent segregation, phase decomposition, and morphology changes in the high-order and low-order groups would falsify short-range order as the primary stabilizing mechanism under the tested conditions.
